outputs.explanation: Panel A is a schematic/table showing breast anatomy and a classification table of breast cancer subtypes; it is not a data plot, so the individual-data-points check does not apply.
Panel B is a conceptual schematic illustrating circadian phenotypes and their relationship to drug sensitivity/tumor growth; no actual data plot is shown.
Panel C is a schematic depicting the experimental setup for measuring circadian rhythms via luciferase recording; not a data plot.

Panel D contains idealized example traces (Model #1-3) used to illustrate the concept of stationary/non-stationary analysis, not real quantified data; per convention this is treated as schematic, so the check does not apply.
Panel E shows an illustrative heatmap used to explain the correlation-analysis workflow, not an actual data heatmap requiring individual points; heatmaps are also exempt from this check.
Panel F shows an idealized example growth-curve schematic (Model 1-3) illustrating the workflow, not measured data requiring individual points; line plots are also exempt.
Panel G shows an idealized dose-response curve schematic illustrating the workflow concept, not real measured data; line plots are exempt from this check.
Panel H is a schematic depicting the genomic analysis workflow with illustrative heatmap/mutation-table icons, not actual data plots requiring individual points.

Panel I contains illustrative example scatter plots (PCA cluster and 3D parameter space) used to conceptually depict subtype definition; these are schematic illustrations of the workflow rather than plotted averages of real data, so the individual-data-points check does not apply.
